subject: Packaging / cap concurrency question — Exhibit C redline and billing mapping
messages:
From: Rachel Blake <rachel.blake@sagemetrics.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@sagemetrics.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Questions on Exhibit C caps/floors and packaging compatibility

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement here has a few follow-ups on the Order Form before we can finalize:

1) Cap/floor aggregation: Exhibit C currently lists a monthly cap and floor but it's not explicit whether those apply at the SKU (per-package) level or aggregated across the whole account. Our billing team needs clarity because SageMetrics will be mixing two package SKUs (Standard + Autoscale). If caps are per-account we may want a different true-up cadence.

2) Packaging discounts + minimums: the draft shows a step discount for bundled packages. Does the discount calculation net against the floor (i.e., does the floor apply after discounts are applied) or before? We need this for our internal forecasting.

3) Migration fallback: if we move 20% of usage from Standard to Autoscale mid-quarter, how is the cap applied for that month — prorated by date, or by aggregated tokens?

I've attached our suggested rate table (SageMetrics_Rate_Table_v3.xlsx) and a lightly redlined order form excerpt. Can you loop in legal and ops for wording that will survive our procurement review?

Goal: get language that preserves your unit economics but is operationally clear for our finance team.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Blake
Head of Procurement, SageMetrics
[Attachment: SageMetrics_Rate_Table_v3.xlsx]

Irene / Marissa — forwarding SageMetrics questions. Key asks below; please propose redline language and ops mapping: 

- Clarify whether monthly cap/floor is applied per SKU or at account level (we usually do account-level aggregation but can support per-SKU with clear operational costs).
- Spell out discount sequencing: are discounts applied before floor calculations? (SageMetrics wants to know for forecasting).
- Migration/proration rules for mid-period SKU moves (they expect prorate-by-date or token-level aggregation).

Attachments from SageMetrics included. If legal can propose two alternatives (account-aggregated default, per-SKU optional with surcharge) that would speed negotiation. Ops: we need a clear billing mapping (how true-ups will show on invoice).

Can we get a redline and a short note for the customer by EOD tomorrow? They want to lock in pricing next week.

Thanks —

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rachel Blake <rachel.blake@sagemetrics.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@sagemetrics.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 18:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on Exhibit C caps/floors and packaging compatibility — proposed redline

Michael / Marissa —

Thanks — I reviewed the draft. Below are our proposed redline points and a recommended compromise position to move this forward:

1) Aggregation of caps/floors (recommended default):
- Proposed language: "Caps and floors set forth in Exhibit C shall be calculated on an account-wide basis across all active SKUs for the applicable billing period; Customer and Company may elect in writing to convert to a per-SKU calculation for a specified SKU for an additional fee as set forth in the rate table."
- Rationale: preserves Redwood's unit economics and keeps billing simple. Offering per-SKU as opt-in gives SageMetrics control if they require it but with predictable cost.

2) Discount sequencing (apply discounts before floor):
- Proposed language: "Volume and packaging discounts shall be applied to gross charges prior to the application of any minimum fee (floor) for the applicable billing period. For clarity, the floor amount is the minimum net charge after the application of discounts and rebates where applicable."
- Rationale: Customer forecasting prefers seeing discounts applied; this also protects Redwood by making the floor an enforceable minimum net revenue.

3) Migration / prorating during billing period:
- Proposed language: "If Customer migrates usage between SKUs during a billing period, Charges shall be calculated on a pro rata basis by days-in-period for the affected SKUs unless otherwise agreed in writing; alternatively, parties may elect to calculate on an aggregated token basis if both parties agree and add such election to the rate table."
- Rationale: default to date-proration for operational simplicity; allow aggregated token election for customers with high intra-period volatility.

4) True-up window and reporting:
- Proposed language: "Company shall provide an itemized true-up statement within thirty (30) days following the close of each billing period; any true-up resulting in a shortfall under the applicable floor shall be invoiced within thirty (30) days thereafter. Disputes to any true-up must be submitted in writing within fourteen (14) days of receipt of the itemized statement."

5) Fallback for legacy packaging discounts:
- Proposed language: "In the event of conflicting discounting language between this Order Form and any prior Master Services Agreement, the Order Form shall control for billing periods covered herein."

I've attached a PDF with the redline applied to Exhibit C and a short comment summary (OrderForm_ExhibitC_redline.pdf). If they push for per-SKU caps with no surcharge, escalate to Dave K (billing) for a commercial exception — we should not accept that as standard.

I'll also mark the per-SKU option with an example surcharge table (e.g., 6% uplift) — Marissa, please coordinate the exact uplift number with Sales Ops.

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OrderForm_ExhibitC_redline.pdf]
